title: Does octave-spaced audiogram curvature improve perceived-hearing prediction? An exploratory cross-cohort test
abstract: Pure-tone averages discard audiogram configuration. We tested a specific nonlinear summary: root-mean-square second differences of bilateral octave-spaced thresholds. Source-only weighted logistic models in 3816 NHANES2011–2012 adults were frozen and evaluated in 4263 separately recruited2015–2016 adults. The comparator used standard ear-level PTA, high-frequency loss, notch summaries and demographic covariates. The concurrent outcome was self-reported hearing trouble. Octave-spaced bilateral audiogram curvature energy changed target weighted Brier score from 0.125382 to 0.125461: difference +0.000080, joint source/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-0.000212,+0.001000]. The registered Brier improvement criterion was not met. This is exploratory same-program cross-cohort evidence, not untouched confirmation, causal physiology or independent-program clinical validation.
